key_idea: Parameterized matching: replace each variable by the distance to its previous occurrence inside the window (0 if first), which makes consistent bijective renaming equal to plain equality; with n <= 2000 all O(n^2) reference windows can be hashed.
sketch: For every start i of the reference, walk j = i..n-1 building a rolling hash of the encoded tokens, where a variable token is encoded as j - prev[j] if prev[j] >= i and 0 otherwise, and a non-variable token by a hash of its text (in a disjoint code space). Store the ~2e6 hashes in a sorted vector. Each query is encoded the same way in one pass and looked up by binary search, so the total is O(n^2 log n + total query length). Pitfalls: a token is a variable only if it is a single LETTER (a lone digit or bracket is a literal); the previous-occurrence code must be relative to the window start; input is up to ~4e6 tokens so use fread-style parsing (cin with std::string took 1.9 s locally, the buffered reader 0.1 s). Stress-tested against a brute-force bijection matcher.
